mainTopic: How far words reach in a נדר: whether 'house' includes the upper story and whether 'bed' includes a דרגש, and what a דרגש is.
overview: This amud has two short משניות about how far a word reaches in a נדר. In the first משנה, רבי מאיר says someone who vows off 'the house' may still use the upper story (עלייה), while חכמים say the upper story counts as part of the house. The גמרא then asks which side two other teachings follow. On the teaching that 'בבית' includes the upper story for נגעים, רב חסדא says it must be רבי מאיר, but אביי shows חכמים could also need that פסוק. On עולא's rule about selling 'a house in my house,' the גמרא suggests רבי מאיר, then reads 'עלייה' as 'the finest room,' so it fits חכמים too. The second משנה has the same argument about whether a vow on a bed includes a דרגש. עולא defines a דרגש as a 'bed of fortune.' רבינא turns away a challenge from the mourning king who reclines on a דרגש. A stronger challenge then comes from the mourner's custom of overturning beds, and the גמרא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: Does a vow on a house include the upper story?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a vow against a house does not include the upper story. חכמים say it does. Everyone agrees that a vow against the upper story does not include the house below.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone vows not to benefit from 'the house,' he may still use the upper story. This is רבי מאיר's view. חכמים say the upper story is part of the house. If someone vows off 'the upper story,' he may use the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a dispute about how far the word 'house' reaches in a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, 'house' means only the main ground-floor building. For חכמים, people include the upper story when they say 'house.' The last case shows the reverse does not work: 'upper story' never includes the house below.
steps.confusionAlert: The dispute only goes one way. Even חכמים agree that 'upper story' does not include the house below. The only question is whether 'house' includes the upper story.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who vows off the house,
is permitted in the upper story; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
The upper story is included in the house.
One who vows off the upper story is permitted in the house.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a vow on a house does not include the upper story. חכמים: it does. Everyone: a vow on the upper story does not include the house.

steps.title: Whose view is the teaching that 'in the house' includes the upper story?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא taught that the word 'בבית' in the laws of נגעים comes to include the יציע and the upper story.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught that the word 'in the house' adds the gallery, and 'in the house' adds the upper story?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching about house-נגעים and asks whose opinion it matches. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That teaching needs an extra word in the פסוק to include the upper story. That suggests its author thinks the upper story is not normally called 'house.' The גמרא wants to know which side of our משנה it belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught? (asking which תנא is the author)
A gallery or half-story attached to the house

phrases.english: GEMARA: Who taught:
'In the house' comes to include the gallery,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק about a נגע in a house, ויקרא 14:35.

phrases.english: 'In the house' comes to include the upper story?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects a teaching about נגעים to the dispute in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side of the משנה's dispute does the teaching that 'בבית' includes the upper story follow?

steps.title: רב חסדא: It must be רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the teaching follows רבי מאיר. For חכמים the upper story is already part of the house, so they would not need a פסוק to include it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי מאיר. If it were חכמים, they already say the upper story is part of the house. So why would they need the word 'in the house' to include it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the teaching belongs to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is that a פסוק is only needed to add something that would not be included otherwise. Only רבי מאיר thinks the upper story is outside 'house,' so only he needs the extra word.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is Rabbi Meir,
for if it were the Rabbis, don't the Rabbis say:
The upper story is included in the house?
Why do I need the verse 'in the house' to include it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who taught it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is רבי מאיר, because חכמים would not need a פסוק to include the upper story.

steps.title: אביי: Even חכמים need the verse
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the teaching could follow חכמים too. The פסוק speaks of 'the land of your possession,' so we might think only rooms attached to the ground count. The extra word teaches that the upper story is included anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even if you say it is חכמים, they still need the פסוק. You might have thought that since it says 'in a house of the land of your possession,' only what is attached to the ground is called a house. The upper story is not attached to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב חסדא's proof. He shows that חכמים also have a reason to need the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In regular speech, חכמים say 'house' includes the upper story. But the laws of נגעים are tied to 'the land,' and that could suggest only ground-level rooms count. So the extra word is needed for נגעים even according to חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind (a wrong first thought)

steps.whatToRemember: A word can be included in everyday speech, like in a נדר, and still need a פסוק for a specific law, like נגעים, where the Torah's wording could suggest otherwise.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Even if you say it is the Rabbis,
a verse is needed.
For it would have entered your mind to say:
'In a house of the land of your possession' is written.
What is attached to the ground is called a house;
the upper story is not attached to the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's claim that only רבי מאיר could need the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that the teaching must follow רבי מאיר. It does not decide that it follows חכמים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב חסדא assumed חכמים would have no reason for the פסוק. But 'the land of your possession' could have suggested excluding rooms not attached to the ground.

steps.title: Whose view is עולא's rule on selling 'a house in my house'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב הונא בר חייא quoting עולא: if a seller says 'I am selling you a house in my house,' he may give the buyer the upper story. It asks whose view this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is the teaching that רב הונא בר חייא said in the name of עולא: 'I am selling you a house in my house' means he can show the buyer the upper story?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second 'whose view?' question about a sales case. This sets up the analysis in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the topic moves from נדרים and נגעים to buying and selling. The key detail is the wording 'a house in my house,' which the גמרא will look at closely next.

keyTerms.meaning: He shows him, meaning he may hand over this room

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: that Rav Huna bar Chiyya said in the name of Ulla:
'A house in my house I am selling you,'
he may show him an upper story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, this time about a sale, tied back to the משנה's dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does עולא's rule on selling 'a house in my house' follow רבי מאיר or חכמים?

steps.title: A plain 'house' would not include the upper story, so it seems to be רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads closely: only because he said 'a house in my house' can he give the upper story. Selling a plain 'house' would not include it. That sounds like רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that he said 'a house that is in my house I am selling you.' But if he said just 'a house,' he may not show him the upper story. Shall we say this is רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from עולא's wording and suggests it matches רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If special wording is needed to reach the upper story, then a plain 'house' must not include it. That is exactly רבי מאיר's view in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is (only because of this detail)
Shall we say? (a suggestion that may be rejected)

phrases.english: The reason is that he said to him:
'A house that is in my house I am selling you.'
But for a plain 'house,' he may not show him an upper story.
Shall we say it is Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes עולא's wording to answer the question of whose view it is.
steps.raayaObject: That עולא's rule follows רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference that a plain 'house' sale does not include the upper story.

steps.title: No: here 'עלייה' means the finest room
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. In עולא's rule, 'עלייה' does not mean upper story. It means the finest of the rooms, so the rule can fit חכמים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say it is חכמים: what does 'עלייה' mean here? The best of the rooms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof by reading the word 'עלייה' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עלייה' is read as coming from 'מעולה,' meaning finest. So 'a house in my house' means he must give the best room. Nothing is being said about the upper story, so there is no proof for רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: What is (what does the word mean here)?

steps.whatToRemember: Both 'whose view' questions end the same way. Each source could fit חכמים too, so neither proves that רבי מאיר's view is needed.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'עלייה' does not mean upper story. It is a play on 'מעולה,' meaning best.

phrases.english: Even if you say it is the Rabbis,
what is the meaning of 'aliyya'?
The finest of the rooms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion that עולא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the link between עולא's rule and רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'עלייה' means upper story, but here it means the finest room.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולא's rule can fit חכמים: 'a house in my house' means the best room.

steps.title: New משנה: Does a vow against a bed include a דרגש?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says someone who vows off a bed may still use a דרגש. חכמים say a דרגש counts as a bed. Everyone agrees that someone who vows off a דרגש may still use a bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone vows not to use a bed, he may use a דרגש. That is רבי מאיר's view. חכמים say a דרגש is included in 'bed.' If someone vows not to use a דרגש, he may use a regular bed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It asks whether the word 'bed' in a vow also covers a special kind of bed called a דרגש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of argument as the earlier house and upper-story case. רבי מאיר reads the vow narrowly, so a דרגש has its own name and is not called a 'bed.' חכמים say people would count it as a bed. Both sides agree the reverse is narrow: 'דרגש' never covers an ordinary bed.

keyTerms.meaning: A special type of bed or couch (the גמרא will discuss exactly what it is)

steps.whyThisMatters: Vows follow how people normally speak. The argument is about whether people would call a דרגש a 'bed.'

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who vows off a bed —
is permitted to use a dargash,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say:
A dargash is included in 'bed.'
One who vows off a dargash — is permitted to use a bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It follows the same pattern as the house and upper-story argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a vow against a bed does not include a דרגש. According to חכמים, it does. A vow against a דרגש does not include a bed.

steps.title: What is a דרגש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what object the משנה means by 'דרגש.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking what a דרגש actually is. This sets up the definition that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot judge whether a דרגש counts as a 'bed' until we know what it is. So the first job is to define the word.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is a dargash?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a key word in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What object does the word דרגש refer to?

steps.title: עולא: A דרגש is a 'bed of good fortune'
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that a דרגש is a bed kept in the house for good luck, not for sleeping.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is a 'bed of good fortune.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question. A דרגש is a bed set up as a sign of good fortune.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to עולא, a דרגש is not a working bed. It is kept as a good-luck object. That explains why רבי מאיר might say people do not call it a 'bed.'

phrases.english: Ulla said:
A bed of fortune.
phrases.notes: He means a bed set up in the house as a good-luck sign, not one that people sleep in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what a דרגש is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A דרגש is a 'bed of fortune,' a bed kept for good luck and not for sleeping.

steps.title: The רבנן challenge עולא from the mourning king
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that at a king's mourning meal everyone sits on the ground and the king reclines on a דרגש. Why would he sit on an unused good-luck bed only on that day?
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to עולא: We learned that when people serve the king the mourner's meal, everyone reclines on the ground and he reclines on the דרגש. All year he does not sit on it, and on that day he does?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן attack עולא's definition. They use a משנה about a king who is in mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a דרגש is a bed nobody uses, it seems strange that the king would start using it on the day of his mourning meal. The רבנן think this shows that a דרגש is a bed people really use.

keyTerms.meaning: Serving the mourner's first meal (סעודת הבראה)

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Ulla:
That which we learned in a mishna:
When they serve him the meal of comfort,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the king. The משנה is talking about a king whose relative has died.

phrases.english: all the people recline on the ground
and he reclines on the dargash.
The whole year he does not sit on it,
and on that day he sits on it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְעוּלָּא, הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's definition of דרגש as an unused good-luck bed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes little sense for a king to begin using a bed he never uses on the very day he is in mourning.

steps.title: רבינא: Just like the meat and wine served that day
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rejects the challenge. On that day we also serve the king meat and wine, which he does not always eat, so special treatment on that day is normal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objects: It is just like meat and wine. All year, if he wants he eats them and if he wants he does not. On that day, we give them to him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends עולא by pushing away the רבנן's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mourner's meal is a day of special honor and comfort. The king gets meat and wine served to him that day, so giving him a special seat on the good-luck bed is not strange either. The question against עולא falls away.

phrases.english: Ravina objects to it:
It is just like meat and wine,
that the whole year, if he wants, he eats,
and if he wants, he does not eat,
yet on that day we give it to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's challenge against עולא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole challenge from the king's mourning meal.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed that unusual treatment on that day was strange. But the mourner's meal brings special treatment anyway, as the meat and wine show.

steps.title: A stronger question: the mourner does not overturn a דרגש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a mourner stands his דרגש on its side and does not overturn it. But another ברייתא says he must overturn every bed in the house. If a דרגש is a bed, why is it different?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is difficult. It was taught: A mourner would not overturn a דרגש, only stand it up. If you say it is a bed of fortune, wasn't it taught that someone who overturns his bed overturns not only his own bed but every bed he has in the house?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first question and brings a stronger one against עולא, from the mourner's custom of overturning beds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mourner must overturn all the beds in his house, even beds nobody sleeps in. If a דרגש is just a good-luck bed, it should be overturned like the others. Yet the ברייתא says it is only stood on its side.

keyTerms.meaning: Overturns (as a mourner does to the beds)
Stands it upright on its side
Rather, this is the real difficulty

phrases.english: Rather, this is difficult:
As it was taught:
A dargash, he would not overturn it,
phrases.notes: 'He' is a mourner, who normally turns his beds over.

phrases.english: but he stands it upright.
And if you say it is a bed of fortune,
wasn't it taught:
One who overturns his bed —
it is not only his own bed that he overturns,
rather, all the beds that he has
inside the house, he overturns!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts aside the rejected question and raises a stronger challenge to עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's definition of דרגש as a bed of fortune.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A mourner overturns every bed in the house, even unused ones. So a good-luck bed should be overturned too, yet the ברייתא says a דרגש is only stood up.

steps.title: The גמרא begins to answer: this is not difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to defend עולא by saying the question is not a problem. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer to the overturning question. This line sets up the explanation, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא has only declared that the challenge can be answered. The actual reason a דרגש is treated differently has not been given yet.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the overturning challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Opening of a defense; the explanation follows.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about overturning a דרגש seems to disprove עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גמרא claims the challenge can be resolved, with details to follow.
